## Comparison

Both traces solve the same state-machine simulation identically, arriving at the same final answer (State=READY, A=false, T=true, n=6, 5 rejections, first at index 5). Their core approaches do not diverge: each steps through all 17 events once, checking allowed states and guards, then applies effects.

The main difference is in **verification density**. Trace 1 re-runs the simulation multiple times—partially re-executing events 1–5, re-reading every allowed-list and guard definition repeatedly, re-summing register histories, and re-tracing state sequences. Trace 2 is more economical: it simulates once, then does targeted spot-checks (step 11, guards, allowed states, first-rejection logic) and a summary table. Neither trace explores alternative branches or introduces ungrounded content, so neither contains CYCLE or MUSE episodes. The extra verification in Trace 1 never changes any result, confirming via the sibling trace that those re-executions added no new information.
